name: VARoleAdvisorNewHomeFurnitureChoice

custom.system_prompt: Greta and Victor are merging households ahead of the wedding and need to choose a mattress for their shared bedroom. They have different firmness preferences and different tolerances for spending on something 'just a mattress'. They ask Sigma to help them find a real compromise rather than one person simply giving in.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Half-unpacked apartment, evening, cardboard boxes shifting, quiet

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Greta and Victor, merging households, need to choose a mattress for their shared bedroom. Greta prefers firm, Victor prefers soft, and Victor is more willing to spend than Greta is. They ask Sigma for help. Sigma asks about their actual sleep habits and complaints, and whether a splittable or adjustable option exists, then helps them find a real compromise instead of one person simply conceding.

user1.name: Greta
user1.tts_prompt: Decisive, slightly impatient with a low-stakes decision dragging on

user2.name: Victor
user2.tts_prompt: Relaxed, willing to spend more than Greta expects

variations.context: Couple merging households ahead of their wedding, disagreeing about mattress firmness and budget

setting.mood: Light-hearted but genuinely unresolved after several failed attempts to agree
setting.relationship_dynamic: Engaged couple negotiating a small but recurring source of friction
setting.background: They've each been sleeping on their own mattress for years and have real, different preferences, not just habit
setting.conversation_style: Teasing, mildly stubborn on both sides, warmer once a concrete option appears

scenario_template.topic: Greta and Victor rehash their mattress firmness disagreement, both citing back or shoulder complaints
scenario_template.note: Should feel like a conversation that has happened before without resolution.

scenario_template.topic: Greta asks Sigma to help them actually resolve this instead of continuing to argue
Sigma asks about specific sleep complaints, sleeping positions, and their actual budget ceiling
scenario_template.note: Both partners answer; Sigma should not favor either preference by default.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma surfaces a real compromise — a dual-firmness or adjustable mattress — and names the trade-off (higher cost) plainly. Both partners' reactions are measured, not instant enthusiasm — at least one of them voices a hedge, a practical worry, or lukewarm acceptance rather than immediate mutual excitement.
scenario_template.note: This should feel like a genuine third option, not Sigma picking a side.

scenario_template.topic: Greta and Victor agree to the compromise, negotiating who covers the extra cost. Keep this grounded — the compromise doesn't have to make both of them equally happy. One partner can sound only partly convinced, or agree more to move on than out of genuine enthusiasm. Avoid both partners sounding fully enthusiastic and resolved.
scenario_template.mood: Warm, amused at how long this took for a mattress
scenario_template.note: Short closing exchange with some humor.

variations.context: Roommates disagree on comfort vs. aesthetics for a shared sofa bed

setting.relationship_dynamic: Engaged couple negotiating a small but recurring source of friction
setting.background: Two roommates deciding on a new sofa bed for their shared living room
setting.conversation_style: Teasing, mildly stubborn on both sides, warmer once a concrete option appears

scenario_template.topic: One prefers a comfortable design while the other prioritizes style.
scenario_template.note: Both have strong opinions and practical concerns.

scenario_template.topic: They ask Sigma to mediate to find a solution that pleases both of them.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be fair here, not decisive.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma inquires about how often they entertain guests and personal space needs.
Sigma suggests a stylish yet practical sofa bed with a reasonable price point.
scenario_template.note: Highlight practical trade-offs identified by Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on the choice, discussing who will pay for the bulk of it.

user1.name: Greta
user1.role: Prefers a firm mattress, more budget-conscious than Victor on this particular purchase, decisive but stuck in a recurring disagreement. Reacts realistically, not with instant enthusiasm — voices at least a little hesitation, a practical worry, or partial reluctance before or even after agreeing; agreement is provisional, not a full conversion to positivity.

user2.name: Victor
user2.role: Prefers a softer mattress, more willing to spend on comfort than Greta, relaxed and willing to compromise. Reacts realistically, not with instant enthusiasm — voices at least a little hesitation, a practical worry, or partial reluctance before or even after agreeing; agreement is provisional, not a full conversion to positivity.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Advisor. Elicits specific sleep complaints and budget from both partners evenly, then surfaces a genuine compromise option rather than favoring either stated preference.

conversation_structure: This is a low-stakes but genuine and recurring disagreement, played with warmth rather than real conflict
Sigma treats both preferences evenly before proposing a compromise
The compromise involves a real trade-off (cost) that the couple still has to negotiate themselves

Human reactions stay realistic and imperfect — hedged agreement, lingering doubt, or one partner less convinced than the other are more natural than universal enthusiasm and a perfectly neat resolution.
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not favor either partner's stated preference by default
Sigma proposes a concrete compromise option rather than asking one person to simply concede
The couple negotiates the remaining detail (who covers extra cost) themselves
